weak.title: Weak scaling, blast lattice L, subcycled
weak.note: Same physics, grid and dt. Owner placement (each refined block on the rank that owns the coarse cells under it, neighbour-first load repair) cuts off-rank traffic 2-7x and lifts the mini-app's np8->np64 efficiency from 0.82 to 0.97, bit-identical results. Refined share at the end: mini-app 30.0%, AMReX 30.3%, MFC 43.9% (MFC with the new tile clustering: 32.5%). np512 runs pending in the batch queue.

conv.title: MFC: subcycled minus lock-step solution vs level-0 dt
conv.note: Plotted: max difference between subcycled and lock-step solutions (not error vs exact). Conservation: subcycled runs within 1.5e-15, lock-step two-level runs within 7.9e-15 (roundoff); 1 and 4 ranks bit-identical. Quartic prolongation (amr_prolong = 2) makes subcycling second order; with regrid, new fine cells must also be seeded with the quartic (fix found by diffing against the mini-app).

cov.title: Refined share of the domain at matched time
cov.note: Coverage of the grid actually used in the last timed steps (regrid after step 220) for every code. MFC required same-level blocks to meet face to face, so each blast became one bounding cube; the new opt-in tile clustering brings MFC to AMReX's refined volume (15.3% vs 15.45%, 29.6% vs 30.25%), currently 4x slower per step until its per-block work is batched.

phase.title: Where MFC's time goes, blast L, 8 GPUs
phase.note: Fill and halo = gather + gfill + halo + seam. Other = swap + rk. Level-0 RHS alone is 80 ms per stage for 8M cells per GPU; the mini-app's whole non-subcycled step is 95 ms.

convm.title: Mini-app: the same test, minmod vs quartic
convm.note: The C/HIP reference implementation found the prolongation limit first (finding F1) and predicted the quartic fix that MFC now confirms.

amr.title: AMR-only cost per coarse step, subcycled (everything except each code's own hydro RHS)
amr.note: Blast lattice L, steps 40-240, everything except each code's own hydro RHS. Audit caveats: MFC rows are single runs and its np8/np64 runs used an earlier build than np512 (same-build reruns in progress); MFC refines more volume (43.9% vs 30%). MFC's flux capture and copies are moved out of its RHS using a 1-GPU estimate that is mostly idle gap; counting kernel time only, MFC subcycled is 0.625/0.917/1.137 s/step. Growth 8->512: mini-app +0.09, AMReX +0.21, PeleC +0.34, MFC +0.51 (two thirds regrid migration).

status.title: Fixes landed (pushed)
items: 6db8415a, 7ccf99b6: subcycling for one and two refined levels; conservative to 1e-15, bit-identical across ranks.
f625519f: amr_tag_abs (AMReX/PeleC tagging, for fair comparisons).
2a970f6e: amr_prolong = 2 quartic ghost prolongation; second-order subcycling.

Pending merge: quartic seeding of new fine cells (restores second order with regrid), tile clustering (matched AMReX coverage), per-block batching.

status.title: Root causes found
items: First-order subcycling with regrid: new fine cells seeded with minmod; found by diffing MFC against the mini-app (post-regrid coarse-fine flux mismatch spiked 50x).
Coverage 1.5x AMReX: MFC required same-level blocks to meet face to face, so each blast became one bounding cube.
Extra AMR cost: host-side per-block work (693 launches and ~8,800 small copies per step vs 81 and 0.5 in the mini-app), not traffic or GPU work.
Subcycled scaling growth: two thirds is regrid migration (device store regrowth and unnecessary moves).
Halo skew: uneven parent-data gathering; owner placement is the fix (mini-app: 0.82 -> 0.97 efficiency at 64 GPUs).
RHS per cell 3.9x the mini-app: MFC's own code (separate MP-WENO pass, copies, host syncs, heavy WENO kernel), not OpenMP or the compiler.
